newsitem.title: INDIA: Hughes sees $1 bln India wireless market.
newsitem.headline: Hughes sees $1 bln India wireless market.

text.p: India could be a $1 billion market for wireless local loop (WLL) services, a senior official of Hughes Network Systems Inc (HNS) said on Thursday.

"When you look at the potential, it is enormous. India is probably a $1 billion market," Arunas Slekys, vice president of HNS's digital cellular networks business unit, told Reuters in the Indian capital.
WLL technology allows a telephone company to use radio waves rather than copper wires to deliver a dialtone to an ordinary phone.
Distinct from cellular phone technology, it can be deployed very quickly as it requires no digging of roads to bury cables.
Hughes Network Systems is a unit of Hughes Electronics Corp, which in turn is a subsidiary of General Motors Corp.
Slekys said India had low telephone density which provided wireless equipment companies with a very attractive market.

He said 80 percent of world's telephones are concentrated in the hands of 20 percent of its population, and in India the ratio was even lower. "We are looking at all of those potential 80 percent and some of those 20 percent," he added.

HNS has been allowed by the Department of Telecommunications to set up a pilot project to demonstrate its WLL technology. A company statement said that the project would soon be set up in the western Indian city of Pune.
"We hope to have a trial run by mid-1998 and hopefully be in business by the end of next year," Slekys said.
HNS also has a joint venture with India's Ispat Industries Ltd, Hughes Ispat Telecom Ltd, which is shortlisted for fixed line licences in the western states of Maharashtra and Karnataka.

Suresh Arora, vice president of Hughes Network Systems said: "In the next five years the wireless services will account for at least 10 percent of all telephones installed in India. We could be looking at a staggering figure of one million subscribers."
Currently less than one percent of the approximately 800 million phone lines in the world are wireless. Hughes said that by 2000 about 20 percent of all lines installed will be wireless.
